/-!
# Erdős Problem 923

*References:*
- [erdosproblems.com/923](https://www.erdosproblems.com/923)
- [Er69b] Erdős, P., *Problems and results in chromatic graph theory*. Proof Techniques in Graph Theory (1969), 27-35.
- [Ro77] Rödl, V., *On the chromatic number of subgraphs of a given graph*. Proc. Amer. Math. Soc. (1977), 370-371.
-/

namespace Erdos923

open SimpleGraph

/--
Is it true that, for every $k$, there is some $f(k)$ such that if $G$ has chromatic number
$\geq f(k)$ then $G$ contains a triangle-free subgraph with chromatic number $\geq k$?

This is true, as shown by Rödl [Ro77].
-/
@[category research solved, AMS 5, formal_proof using lean4 at "https://github.com/plby/lean-proofs/blob/main/src/v4.29.1/ErdosProblems/Erdos923.lean"]
theorem erdos_923 : answer(True) ↔ ∀ (V : Type*) (n : ℕ),
    ∃ k : ℕ, ∀ G : SimpleGraph V, k ≤ G.chromaticNumber →
    ∃ H ≤ G, n ≤ H.chromaticNumber ∧ H.CliqueFree 3 := by
  sorry

end Erdos923

reformulations.difference: Lean permits the threshold k to depend on the vertex type V and quantifies over infinite as well as finite vertex types, whereas the source presents a graph-uniform function f(n).
reformulations.equivalence_argument: The local assertion on one fixed countably infinite type suffices to recover a common bound for all finite graphs. Apply it with target n+2, embed any finite graph into that type, and restrict the resulting triangle-free subgraph back to the finite vertices. A q-coloring of the restriction extends to a (q+1)-coloring of the padded graph, so the restriction has chromatic number at least n. Conversely, finite-coloring compactness ensures that any graph with chromatic number at least a finite k has a finite induced subgraph with chromatic number at least k. Thus a common finite-graph bound extends to arbitrary vertex types. A uniform bound trivially specializes to each V. Proved independently of the reviewed theorem in /workspace/review/equivalence.lean as local_iff_uniform, local_iff_finite, and local_iff_source; their axioms contain no sorryAx.

reformulations.difference: The witness H ≤ G has the same vertex type as G, while Rödl explicitly allows a subgraph to have a smaller vertex set.
reformulations.equivalence_argument: Every H ≤ G is an ordinary spanning subgraph. Conversely, extend any ordinary subgraph to the ambient vertex set by adding isolated vertices. This creates no triangles and cannot decrease its chromatic number, so the lower bound n ≤ χ(H) is preserved, including empty-graph cases. Proved for every G and n as spanning_iff_subgraph in /workspace/review/equivalence.lean, with only standard Lean axioms.
